title: A Misinformation Test for Social Media

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我在《纽约时报》的每日简报栏目 DealBook 负责商业和政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场采访商界、政界和文化界最具影响力的领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的实时对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将于11月18日在 nytimes.com 上直播精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你不会想错过它的。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天是。

sentences.en: The nation's biggest social media companies are determined to avoid the mistakes that they made during the 2016 election.
sentences.zh: 美国最大的社交媒体公司决心避免他们在2016年大选中犯下的错误。

sentences.en: But in the process, they've ignited a different kind of firestorm.
sentences.zh: 但在这一过程中，他们引发了一场不同性质的风暴。

sentences.en: My colleague, Kevin Roos, reports from San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 我的同事凯文·罗斯从旧金山发回报道。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, October 21St.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月21日，星期三。

sentences.en: You know, Kevin, actually, it's been ages since we had you on the show.
sentences.zh: 你知道，凯文，其实我们已经很久没有请你上节目了。

sentences.en: Ages?
sentences.zh: 很久？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I wonder whose fault that is.
sentences.zh: 我在想这该怪谁。

sentences.en: You don't call.
sentences.zh: 你不打电话。

sentences.en: You don't write.
sentences.zh: 也不写信。

sentences.en: I thought we had something.
sentences.zh: 我还以为我们曾有过什么呢。

sentences.en: No, I think that you didn't intersect with the news.
sentences.zh: 不，我觉得是你没有跟新闻产生交集。

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 这倒也是。

sentences.en: But here you are, intersecting.
sentences.zh: 但现在你来了，产生了交集。

sentences.en: There's been a lot going on.
sentences.zh: 发生了挺多事的。

sentences.en: So, Kevin, my sense is that the big social media companies, which you have been covering for a really long time,
sentences.zh: 所以，凯文，我的感觉是，你长期报道的这些大型社交媒体公司，

sentences.en: have been preparing very diligently, very carefully, very expensively for the 2020 election and for the possibility of a major moment of misinformation,
sentences.zh: 一直在为2020年大选做着非常勤勉、非常仔细、投入巨大的准备，以防范可能出现的重大虚假信息时刻，

sentences.en: for some kind of act of interference, given how much they failed to do that back in 2016.
sentences.zh: 鉴于他们在2016年时在这方面做得多么不到位，他们需要防范某种干扰行为。

sentences.en: So, I want you to summarize what the preparations that they have been doing have looked like.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想请你总结一下他们所做的准备工作是什么样的。

sentences.en: So, since 2016, these three big social media companies, Facebook, Twitter, YouTube, they've spent tons of time and money
sentences.zh: 所以，自2016年以来，这三家大型社交媒体公司——Facebook、Twitter、YouTube——投入了大量的时间和资金，

sentences.en: investing in trying to keep foreign interference from happening on their platform again.
sentences.zh: 投资于试图阻止外国干预再次在他们的平台上发生。

sentences.en: There have been new policies, new teams, they've hired tons of new people and moderators.
sentences.zh: 他们制定了新政策，组建了新团队，雇用了大量新员工和审核员。

sentences.en: And basically, their goal is to just avoid being played again, to avoid the kind of foreign interference attempt that they were seen as having allowed on their platforms in 2016.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们的目标就是避免再次被耍，避免2016年被认为在其平台上允许的那类外国干预企图再次发生。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And my sense is that beyond just being alert to this, they want to be more responsive, right?
sentences.zh: 我的感觉是，除了对此保持警惕之外，他们还希望反应更灵敏，对吧？

sentences.en: They want to be less hands-off.
sentences.zh: 他们不希望再采取放任不管的态度。

sentences.en: So, if something happens, the goal is not just to notice it, but to actually do something.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果发生什么事，目标不仅是注意到它，还要真正采取行动。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: They want to act in a way that is consistent with their policies, but also that is fast,
sentences.zh: 他们的行动既要符合其政策，又要迅速，

sentences.en: that gets to these problems before they spiral out of control and become huge election interference issues.
sentences.zh: 在问题失控并演变成重大选举干扰问题之前解决掉它们。

sentences.en: It's not just what they do, it's also how quickly they're able to do it.
sentences.zh: 这不仅关乎他们做什么，还关乎他们能以多快的速度去做。

sentences.en: So, I guess in a sense, in the weeks leading up to the election, they are kind of just waiting for the first big test case for these systeMs.
sentences.zh: 所以我想从某种意义上说，在选举前的几周里，他们其实就是在等待这些系统的第一次重大考验。

sentences.en: Yeah, but the kind of fear that they've had is this kind of October surprise, this introduction of something new,
sentences.zh: 是的，但他们一直以来的恐惧是那种“十月惊奇”，也就是引入某些新东西，

sentences.en: some attempt to kind of steer the narrative about the election at the last possible moment.
sentences.zh: 某种试图在最后关头左右选举叙事的企图。

sentences.en: And that came for them last week in the form of this New York Post article that appeared on Wednesday morning.
sentences.zh: 而上周三上午发表的那篇《纽约派驻》文章，对他们来说就是这种情况。

sentences.en: And in broad strokes, what was this?
sentences.zh: 大体上讲，这到底是什么？

sentences.en: So, at a sort of broad level, what the Post publishes is a story alleging that there's this laptop that was used by Hunter Biden, the son of Joe Biden, presidential candidate,
sentences.zh: 所以，从宏观层面来看，《纽约邮报》发表了一篇报道，声称有一台笔记本电脑曾被美国总统候选人乔·拜登的儿子亨特·拜登使用过，

sentences.en: that made its way to investigators and ultimately to Rudy Giuliani, the president's lawyer.
sentences.zh: 这台电脑辗转到了调查人员手中，最终交给了总统的律师鲁迪·朱利安尼。

sentences.en: And that when they inspected this computer, it had emails on it that the Post described as being incriminating.
sentences.zh: 当他们检查这台电脑时，里面有《邮报》形容为具有 incriminating（定罪证据）性质的电子邮件。

sentences.en: Now, there are still lots of questions about these emails.
sentences.zh: 现在，关于这些电子邮件仍然有很多疑问。

sentences.en: We have not been able to verify their authenticity.
sentences.zh: 我们还没能核实它们的真实性。

sentences.en: We don't know who actually got access to them and how they made their way up to Rudy Giuliani.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道究竟是谁接触到了它们，又是如何流转到鲁迪·朱利安尼手里的。

sentences.en: There are still so many questions about the provenance of these materials and whether or not they're real.
sentences.zh: 关于这些材料的来源以及它们是否真实，依然存在无数的疑问。

sentences.en: But that's just the sort of nutshell version of what the Post publishes on Wednesday morning.
sentences.zh: 但这只是《邮报》周三上午发表的内容的简要概述。

sentences.en: And so what are the big social media companies, the three you identified, Twitter, Facebook, YouTube, what are they thinking in their very well-prepared offices about this story?
sentences.zh: 那么，各大社交媒体公司——你提到的那三家，Twitter、Facebook、YouTube——在他们准备充分的办公室里，对这篇报道是怎么想的呢？

sentences.en: Well, I've spoken to some people at the companies and basically what they were thinking is, here we go again.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我和公司里的一些人聊过，基本上他们的想法是：又来了。

sentences.en: To them, it seemed to have a lot of the same hallmarks as the 2016 hack and leak campaign that Russia carried out,
sentences.zh: 在他们看来，这与俄罗斯在2016年实施的黑客攻击和泄密活动有很多相同的特征，

sentences.en: where they hacked into email inboxes belonging to prominent Democrats and released those emails in a coordinated fashion to try to steer the discussion around that year's election.
sentences.zh: 当时黑客入侵了民主党显要人物的电子邮箱，并以协调一致的方式发布了这些邮件，试图左右当年选举的讨论方向。

sentences.en: And so the way that these platforms think about threats like this, they basically have three options for what to do next.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些平台在考虑此类威胁时，接下来基本上有三种选择。

sentences.en: They can do nothing.
sentences.zh: 他们可以什么都不做。

sentences.en: They can let this story run its course and trust that, you know, people will work out the facts and that the systems will work as designed.
sentences.zh: 他们可以让这篇报道顺其自然，相信人们会弄清事实，系统也会按设计的那样运作。

sentences.en: They can step in really aggressively and essentially ban the story from their platforms and say, we're going to take this down.
sentences.zh: 他们可以采取非常强硬的干预措施，基本上在平台上封禁这篇报道，并宣布：“我们要把它撤下。”

sentences.en: We're not going to put any links to it.
sentences.zh: “我们不会提供任何指向它的链接。”

sentences.en: You're not going to be allowed to link to it.
sentences.zh: “你们将不被允许链接到它。”

sentences.en: And we're going to lock your account if you do link to it.
sentences.zh: “如果你链接了它，我们将锁定你的账户。”

sentences.en: And that's sort of the nuclear option.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是终极核选项。

sentences.en: And then there's all these decisions that they can make in the middle of that, between doing nothing and taking it down.
sentences.zh: 此外，在什么都不做和彻底删除之间，他们还可以做出各种折中的决定。

sentences.en: And those would include things like putting a label on it or putting a little fact check underneath it or reducing its distribution through their algorithms rather than banning it outright.
sentences.zh: 其中包括诸如给它贴上标签、在下方添加一点事实核查，或者通过算法降低其分发量，而不是直接全面封禁。

sentences.en: And these platforms know that they have to do something quickly and that whatever decision they make, the longer they wait,
sentences.zh: 这些平台知道他们必须迅速采取行动，而且无论做出什么决定，他们等的时间越长，

sentences.en: the harder it's going to get to restrain or to reel in this narrative that is already starting to go viral.
sentences.zh: 想要遏制或收回已经开始病毒式传播的这套叙事就会越困难。

sentences.en: So how did these companies react in that very short period of time?
sentences.zh: 那么，这些公司在那么短的时间内是如何反应的？

sentences.en: What did each of them do?
sentences.zh: 他们各自都做了什么？

sentences.en: So the initial reaction from these platforms is a little bit all over the place.
sentences.zh: 所以这些平台的最初反应有点五花八门。

sentences.en: So YouTube basically does nothing.
sentences.zh: YouTube 基本上什么也没做。

sentences.en: It says, given what we know about it right now, this story is allowed on YouTube and we'll continue to evaluate it.
sentences.zh: 它表示，鉴于我们目前对其的了解，这篇报道在 YouTube 上是允许存在的，我们将继续对其进行评估。

sentences.en: Next, we have Facebook.
sentences.zh: 接下来是 Facebook。

sentences.en: And they basically come out several hours after this story is posted.
sentences.zh: 他们在报道发布几小时后基本上做出了表态。

sentences.en: And they say that they are going to demote the story, basically slow its spread in their algorithms until it can be evaluated by third-party fact checkers.
sentences.zh: 他们表示将对这篇报道进行降权处理，也就是在算法中放慢其传播速度，直到第三方事实核查机构对其进行评估。

sentences.en: So they're basically saying, we're going to pump the brakes on this story until the people that we trust to determine whether or not these things are true or not can look at it.
sentences.zh: 所以他们基本上是说：“我们要给这篇报道踩刹车，直到我们信任的、能判断这些事情真伪的人来审视它。”

sentences.en: So they don't block it.
sentences.zh: 所以他们没有封锁它。

sentences.en: They're just kind of throwing a sheet over it.
sentences.zh: 他们只是给它盖上了一层布。

sentences.en: They're not blocking it.
sentences.zh: 他们没有封锁它。

sentences.en: They're just kind of putting it on ice for the moment.
sentences.zh: 他们只是暂时把它搁置起来。

sentences.en: And then you have Twitter, which makes the most aggressive call in the early hours after this story is posted.
sentences.zh: 然后是 Twitter，在报道发布后的头几个小时里，它做出了最激进的决定。

sentences.en: And they say that we are not even going to allow people to link to this story because this violates our rules against sharing private information because there were some sort of private information contained in these emails that the post had excerpted.
sentences.zh: 他们表示，甚至不允许人们链接到这篇报道，因为这违反了我们关于分享私人信息的规定，因为《邮报》节选的这些邮件中包含了一些私人信息。

sentences.en: And that also it was a violation of their hacked materials policy.
sentences.zh: 而且这也违反了他们的黑客材料政策。

sentences.en: So they were basically treating this as if it were a hacker sharing some passwords that they had gotten from some data dump.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们基本上把这当作黑客分享从某些数据转储中获取的密码来处理。

sentences.en: So Twitter is taking the kind of nuclear option, as you described it.
sentences.zh: 所以正如你所描述的那样，Twitter 采取了类似核选项的措施。

sentences.en: Not only is Twitter banning people from linking to this story, but it's locking the accounts of the people who do link to it.
sentences.zh: Twitter 不仅禁止人们链接到这篇报道，还锁定了链接到该报道的人的账户。

sentences.en: Including some pretty prominent people like Kayleigh McEnany, the White House press secretary.
sentences.zh: 其中包括一些相当知名的人物，比如白宫新闻秘书凯莉·麦克纳尼。

sentences.en: And for Twitter, like, this is a pretty big enforcement action.
sentences.zh: 对 Twitter 来说，这算是一个相当大的执法行动。

sentences.en: And they're basically taking no chances with this.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上不给这件事留任何侥幸余地。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So they are choosing to do the exact thing that everyone said social media companies did not do in 2016 when information began circulating of dubious origin.
sentences.zh: 所以他们选择做的，恰恰是每个人都说社交媒体公司在2016年有来源可疑的信息开始流传时没有做的事情。

sentences.en: For example, John Podesta's emails.
sentences.zh: 例如，约翰·波多斯间的电子邮件。

sentences.en: They are just clipping its wings.
sentences.zh: 他们只是剪断它的翅膀。

sentences.en: They are making sure it cannot be shared.
sentences.zh: 他们确保它无法被分享。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And their theory on why they're doing this is that it's better for them to act too aggressively and let up later than to let something go and then try to catch up to it.
sentences.zh: 他们这样做的理论依据是：宁可行动过于激进、事后再放松，也总比放任不管再去追赶要好。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And so, Kevin, what is the reaction to this decision by these companies?
sentences.zh: 那么，凯文，外界对这些公司的这一决定有什么反应？

sentences.en: So among many people, including a lot of people on the left, frankly,
sentences.zh: 在许多人当中，坦白说包括很多左翼人士，

sentences.en: there was relief that after years of criticism for not having done enough to stop interference in the 2016 election,
sentences.zh: 人们感到一种如释重负，因为在经历多年来因未能采取足够措施阻止2016年大选干预而遭受的批评之后，

sentences.en: that they were being attentive and proactive and doing something rather than nothing to avert a potential similar crisis this year.
sentences.zh: 他们终于表现得专注、主动，采取了行动而不是无所作为，以避免今年可能发生的类似危机。

sentences.en: But then...
sentences.zh: 但随后……

sentences.en: This is a dark moment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个黑暗的时刻。

sentences.en: There were people, many on the right.
sentences.zh: 也有人，其中很多是右翼人士。

sentences.en: This was mass censorship on a scale that America has never experienced, not in 245 years.
sentences.zh: 这是美国245年来从未经历过的大规模审查。

sentences.en: It's both insidious and infuriating.
sentences.zh: 既阴险又令人愤怒。

sentences.en: Who were very offended by these decisions, by the platforMs.
sentences.zh: 他们对这些平台的决定感到非常冒犯。

sentences.en: Make no mistake, Twitter, Facebook, they are not arbiters of truth.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，Twitter 和 Facebook 并非真理的仲裁者。

sentences.en: They're all engaging in censorship, so you're kept in the dark.
sentences.zh: 它们都在进行审查，好让你们被蒙在鼓里。

sentences.en: Cold, calculated political actors.
sentences.zh: 冷血、算计的政治玩家。

sentences.en: Josh Hawley, the senator from Missouri, one of the sort of most vocal critics of these big tech platforms, came out.
sentences.zh: 密苏里州参议员乔什·霍利，作为大型科技平台最直言不讳的批评者之一，站了出来。

sentences.en: If Republicans don't stand up and do something about this, these companies are going to run this country.
sentences.zh: 如果共和党人不站出来采取行动，这些公司就要统治这个国家了。

sentences.en: And said that this was the dawn of a dangerous new era in American history.
sentences.zh: 并称这是美国历史上一个危险新时代的开始。

sentences.en: Silencing the media is a direct violation of the principles of the First Amendment.
sentences.zh: 压制媒体是对第一修正案原则的直接践踏。

sentences.en: Ted Cruz, senator from Texas, also said that this was an affront to free speech.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州参议员特德·克鲁兹也表示，这是对言论自由的侮辱。

sentences.en: We're seeing Silicon Valley billionaires, frankly, drunk with power.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，我们看到硅谷的亿万富翁们被权力冲昏了头脑。

sentences.en: So, the entire sort of Republican establishment goes nuts over this.
sentences.zh: 因此，整个共和党建制派对此陷入了疯狂。

sentences.en: They are calling for subpoenas against the leaders of Twitter and Facebook.
sentences.zh: 他们呼吁对 Twitter 和 Facebook 的领导人发出传票。

sentences.en: The Senate Republicans need to ask Jack Dorsey, what is your policy so we can decide whether or not we're going to start regulating this?
sentences.zh: 参议院共和党人需要问问杰克·多西，你的政策是什么，这样我们才能决定是否要开始对你进行监管。

sentences.en: They are calling for legal protections for these platforms to be revoked.
sentences.zh: 他们呼吁撤销对这些平台的法律保护。

sentences.en: You're not a real platform.
sentences.zh: 你根本不是个真正的平台。

sentences.en: You're just another liberal editor.
sentences.zh: 你不过是又一个自由派编辑。

sentences.en: And they are essentially treating these companies as if they are themselves interfering in a U.S.
sentences.zh: 他们实质上是将这些公司视为自身正在干预美国大选，

sentences.en: election by acting to prevent a possible interference attempt.
sentences.zh: 而它们的行为是为了阻止可能的干预企图。

sentences.en: And let me be very clear.
sentences.zh: 让我说得非常清楚。

sentences.en: Twitter is interfering in this election.
sentences.zh: Twitter 正在干预这次大选。

sentences.en: Big tech.
sentences.zh: 科技巨头。

sentences.en: They want to run America.
sentences.zh: 他们想统治美国。

sentences.en: We've got to stop them.
sentences.zh: 我们必须阻止他们。

sentences.en: We've got to do something right now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在就得采取行动。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: They are interfering by trying to stop interference.
sentences.zh: 他们通过试图阻止干预来进行干预。

sentences.en: It's complicated.
sentences.zh: 这很复杂。

sentences.en: Very, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常复杂。

sentences.en: The whole thing is crazy.
sentences.zh: 整件事太疯狂了。

sentences.en: And, of course, finally, the president himself weighs in.
sentences.zh: 当然，最后总统本人也介入了。

sentences.en: And it's like maybe a first arm of the DNC.
sentences.zh: 这简直就像是民主党全国委员会的第一个分支。

sentences.en: And attacks these companies, repeats his call for the repeal of these legal protections that these companies have.
sentences.zh: 他攻击这些公司，并重申要求废除这些公司享有的法律保护。

sentences.en: But it's going to all end up in a big lawsuit and there are things that can happen that are very severe.
sentences.zh: 但这最终都会演变成一场官司，而且可能会发生非常严重的事情。

sentences.en: And basically says that they are trying to rig the election for Joe Biden by suppressing this story.
sentences.zh: 他基本上说，他们试图通过压制这篇报道来为乔·拜登操纵大选。

sentences.en: So this does not go smoothly.
sentences.zh: 所以这进展得并不顺利。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: It's kind of a damned if you do, damned if you don't situation for them where they're criticized for not doing enough to protect against election interference.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，这有点像左右为难的困境：如果不采取足够的措施来防范选举干扰，他们会受到批评。

sentences.en: But then when they try to act to protect against potential election interference, they're criticized for that, too.
sentences.zh: 但当他们试图采取行动防范潜在的选举干扰时，他们又会因此受到批评。

sentences.en: So all this criticism, all these questions surrounding this story really leads them to try to figure out, like, did we make the right call here?
sentences.zh: 因此，所有这些批评，围绕这篇报道的所有疑问，实际上让他们开始琢磨：我们这次是不是做错了决定？

sentences.en: And essentially, Facebook and YouTube sort of stick by their decisions.
sentences.zh: 从根本上说，Facebook和YouTube算是坚持了他们的决定。

sentences.en: Like, YouTube doesn't take down content.
sentences.zh: 比如，YouTube没有删除内容。

sentences.en: Facebook continues to kind of limit this content without blocking it entirely.
sentences.zh: Facebook继续限制这类内容，但没有完全屏蔽。

sentences.en: But Twitter starts actually reversing its original decision.
sentences.zh: 但Twitter开始实际推翻其最初的决定。

sentences.en: They sort of land on this position of, we think that this article is being so widely discussed that we no longer think it makes sense to block links to it.
sentences.zh: 他们的立场大致变成了：我们认为这篇文章引发了极其广泛的讨论，因此我们不再认为屏蔽指向它的链接是合理的。

sentences.en: But in the future, we will put labels on materials that might have been hacked.
sentences.zh: 但在未来，我们会给可能被黑客攻击的材料贴上标签。

sentences.en: So we will essentially take a middle ground position on stories like this in the future.
sentences.zh: 所以我们今后对这类报道基本上会采取中间立场。

sentences.en: And I think from the platform's point of view, this story and the issues it raised were actually a little more complicated than they originally thought.
sentences.zh: 我认为从平台的角度来看，这篇报道以及它引发的问题实际上比他们最初想象的要复杂一些。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》App？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 免费畅读？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费体验《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡，会怎么样？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》App时，你在App内的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》App，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So Kevin, what made this New York Post story, as you just said, such a uniquely complicated situation for these big social media companies?
sentences.zh: 那么，凯文，正如你刚才所说，是什么让这篇《纽约 Post》的报道对这些大型社交媒体公司来说是一个如此独特的复杂情况？

sentences.en: So I think all the platforms, Facebook, YouTube, Twitter, would agree that foreign election interference is bad.
sentences.zh: 我认为所有的平台——Facebook、YouTube、Twitter——都会同意外国选举干扰是不好的。

sentences.en: And that it's part of their job and something they're very committed to doing is stopping foreign interference attempts.
sentences.zh: 阻止外国干扰尝试是他们工作的一部分，也是他们坚定不移致力于去做的事情。

sentences.en: But foreign election interference is not always very obvious.
sentences.zh: 但外国选举干扰并不总是那么明显。

sentences.en: So in 2016, you had trolls in St. Petersburg who were literally buying Facebook ads in rubles.
sentences.zh: 所以在2016年，圣彼得堡的那些水军实际上是用卢布购买Facebook广告。

sentences.en: But there are much more subtle ways that a government or an entity could try to influence a U.S.
sentences.zh: 但政府或实体可能会用更隐蔽的方式来试图影响美国的

sentences.en: election.
sentences.zh: 选举。

sentences.en: And one possibility is that they could use a hack and leak operation where they steal information and then distribute it.
sentences.zh: 其中一种可能性是，他们可能会使用黑客攻击和泄露行动，即窃取信息然后进行分发。

sentences.en: But instead of going directly out with it or through an organization like WikiLeaks, they could go through a major American news organization like the New York PoSt.
sentences.zh: 但他们不直接公开发布，也不通过维基解密这样的组织，而是通过《纽约邮报》这样的大型美国新闻机构。

sentences.en: And these platforms, they don't find it particularly hard to take action against sort of cyber attacks and things that are, you know,
sentences.zh: 对于网络攻击以及那些，你知道的，

sentences.en: pretty blatantly trying to manipulate their services.
sentences.zh: 明目张胆试图操纵其服务的行为，这些平台并不觉得采取行动有多么困难。

sentences.en: But in this case, it's more like trying to figure out if the New York Post can be trusted or not, which is a very uncomfortable position for them to be in.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，它更像是去弄清楚《纽约邮报》是否值得信任，这让他们处于一个非常尴尬的境地。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because all of a sudden, a company like Twitter or Facebook would suddenly be in the position, perhaps throughout an election,
sentences.zh: 因为突然之间，像Twitter或Facebook这样的公司可能会在整个选举期间陷入这样一种境地：

sentences.en: of routinely deciding whose confidential sources are trustworthy and whose articles based on documents should be allowed to have their links shared or blocked.
sentences.zh: 它们必须例行公事般地决定，谁的机密消息来源是可信的，谁基于文件的文章应该被允许分享链接或遭到屏蔽。

sentences.en: And that could become a pretty slippery slope pretty quickly.
sentences.zh: 这很快就会演变成一条非常危险的滑坡。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And after Twitter made its decision to block links to the New York Post story, they heard from a lot of journalists, not just in the U.S., but around the world,
sentences.zh: 在Twitter做出屏蔽指向《纽约邮报》报道的链接的决定后，他们听到了许多记者的声音，不仅在美国，还有世界各地，

sentences.en: who worried that this policy against not allowing links to hacked materials could endanger their ability to report on things involving confidential sources and whistleblowers.
sentences.zh: 他们担心这种不允许分享被黑材料链接的政策可能会危及他们报道涉及机密消息来源和吹哨人的事件的能力。

sentences.en: And that's part of the reason that they walked back their initial call.
sentences.zh: 这也是他们收回最初决定的部分原因。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, at the end of the day, I think it's safe to say we don't want social media companies to be the gatekeepers of journalism.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，归根结底，我们可以肯定地说，我们不希望社交媒体公司成为新闻业的把关人。

sentences.en: We want journalists to produce good journalism that applies careful standards and thoughtful judgments to what information gets out and where it comes from.
sentences.zh: 我们希望记者能够产出优秀的新闻，对信息的来源和流向进行严谨的标准审视和深思熟虑的判断。

sentences.en: And I guess this is still an open question.
sentences.zh: 我想这仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。

sentences.en: The New York Post may not have done that in this case.
sentences.zh: 《纽约邮报》在这种情况下可能并没有做到这一点。

sentences.en: There's still a lot we don't know, to be clear.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，还有很多事情是我们不知道的。

sentences.en: I mean, our colleagues have done some reporting and there seem to be some sort of red flags in the process behind this particular story.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们的同事做了一些报道，在这个特定报道背后的运作过程中似乎存在某种危险信号。

sentences.en: Apparently, the reporter who wrote most of the story didn't want his byline attached to it, things like that.
sentences.zh: 显然，写了这篇报道大部分内容的记者不想把他的署名挂在上面，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Not a good sign.
sentences.zh: 这不是个好兆头。

sentences.en: Not a good sign.
sentences.zh: 这不是个好兆头。

sentences.en: So very unorthodox process behind this story.
sentences.zh: 所以这篇报道背后的运作过程非常不常规。

sentences.en: But I think it does point to the fact that these platforms are reluctantly being asked to not just sort of keep their platforms from being manipulated, but in cases like this,
sentences.zh: 但我认为这确实说明了一个事实：这些平台极其不情愿地被要求不仅要防止其平台被操纵，而且在像这样的一些情况下，

sentences.en: to kind of referee journalism in a way that they're very uncomfortable doing.
sentences.zh: 还要以一种让他们感到极度不舒服的方式来对新闻业进行裁判。

sentences.en: And that arguably shouldn't be their job at all.
sentences.zh: 可以说，这根本不应该是他们的工作。

sentences.en: But because of the nature of these hack and leak campaigns, they sometimes have to be.
sentences.zh: 但由于这些黑客攻击和泄露行动的性质，他们有时不得不这样做。

sentences.en: Kevin, listening to you, I'm wondering, are these social media companies and their policies on this kind of content,
sentences.zh: 凯文，听了你的话，我在想，这些社交媒体公司及其针对此类内容的政策，

sentences.en: are they making journalists approach this with greater rigor and perhaps with the fear that they would publish something that would be blocked or deplatformed?
sentences.zh: 是否正在促使记者以更严谨的态度来对待此事，或许也带着一种发表了会被屏蔽或封号的内容的恐惧？

sentences.en: And would that become an incentive for everyone in the news media, who of course wants their content to be shared, to behave better?
sentences.zh: 这是否会成为新闻媒体中所有人都表现得更好的动力——当然，每个人都希望自己的内容被分享？

sentences.en: I don't think the platform set out to improve journalism.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这些平台出发点是为了改善新闻业。

sentences.en: I don't think that's one of their sort of goals here.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这是他们在这里的目标之一。

sentences.en: But I think in this case, they may actually have done reporters a favor by coming out early and aggressively to say there is something fishy about this story.
sentences.zh: 但我认为在这种情况下，他们可能确实帮了记者一个忙，因为他们很早就强势地站出来说，这篇报道有些可疑。

sentences.en: And their decision to act on it changed the tenor of some of the coverage that followed.
sentences.zh: 他们采取行动的决定改变了随后部分报道的基调。

sentences.en: Instead of just repeating what was in these alleged emails,
sentences.zh: 报道的内容不再只是重复那些所谓的电子邮件中的内容，

sentences.en: the story became sort of about process and journalistic rigor and platform governance and all of these sort of meta topics that I think ultimately shed more light on what happened than just going back through the emails and printing the most salacious parts.
sentences.zh: 而是变成了关于运作过程、新闻严谨性、平台治理以及所有这些元话题，我认为这些话题最终比重新翻看电子邮件并打印出最耸人听闻的部分，更能阐明事情的真相。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that's very different from what happened in 2016 when the emails stolen from the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 这与2016年民主党电子邮件被盗时发生的情况截然不同。

sentences.en: And again, we don't know if any emails were stolen from anybody in this case.
sentences.zh: 同样，我们不知道这次是否有任何人的电子邮件被盗。

sentences.en: But back in 2016, those emails were made public and news organizations, including The New York Times, including me as a reporter,
sentences.zh: 但在2016年，那些电子邮件被公之于众，包括《纽约时报》在内的新闻机构——包括我作为一名记者——

sentences.en: went through them and generated stories about them.
sentences.zh: 都仔细查阅了这些邮件并生成了相关报道。

sentences.en: And it wasn't about where they had come from.
sentences.zh: 重点不在于它们是从哪里来的。

sentences.en: It was about what they had revealed about the characters in the emails.
sentences.zh: 重点在于它们揭示了邮件中人物的什么信息。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think that points to one of the major shifts that has happened since 2016.
sentences.zh: 我认为这指出了自2016年以来发生的重大转变之一。

sentences.en: It's not just the platforms that have been worried about a repeat hack and leak operation and making plans for what they're going to do.
sentences.zh: 不仅是平台一直在担心重演黑客攻击和泄露行动并制定应对计划。

sentences.en: It's also news organizations.
sentences.zh: 新闻机构也是如此。

sentences.en: At the Times,
sentences.zh: 在《时报》，

sentences.en: like I and a group of other disinformation reporters and researchers put together a list of guidelines for how we would handle a hack and leak that resembled the one we saw in 2016.
sentences.zh: 我和其他几位虚假信息记者及研究人员一起制定了一套指导方针，说明如果我们遇到类似于2016年那样的黑客攻击和泄露事件，我们将如何处理。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And is there anything you can say about that process?
sentences.zh: 关于这个运作过程，你有什么能说的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's a five-step process.
sentences.zh: 这是一个五步流程。

sentences.en: And we gave it a silly acronym.
sentences.zh: 我们给它起了一个有点傻的缩写。

sentences.en: It's the email method.
sentences.zh: 也就是“邮件”（email）方法。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So there's evidence, motive, activity, intent, and labels.
sentences.zh: 也就是证据（evidence）、动机（motive）、活动（activity）、意图（intent）和标签（labels）。

sentences.en: And it's just the kind of thing that we are considering internally as sort of a checklist for the process that we go through when something like a hack and leak does emerge.
sentences.zh: 当类似黑客攻击和泄露事件出现时，这正是我们在内部作为核对清单来考虑的一套流程。

sentences.en: Kevin, I'm curious if all the diligence from these news organizations like The Times and the crackdown by the big social media companies on this New York Post story, did it work?
sentences.zh: 凯文，我很好奇，来自《时报》等新闻机构的所有严谨审查以及大型社交媒体公司对这篇《纽约邮报》报道的打击，真的起作用了吗？

sentences.en: Did it, at the end of the day, limit the reach of this story whose origins we are still trying to figure out and which are suspicious?
sentences.zh: 归根结底，它是否限制了这篇报道的传播范围？我们至今仍在试图弄清这篇报道的来源，而且其来源十分可疑。

sentences.en: Yes and no.
sentences.zh: 怎么说呢，既有作用又没起作用。

sentences.en: I think just in pure statistical terms, like the story still traveled very widely.
sentences.zh: 我认为仅从纯粹的统计数据来看，这篇报道的传播依然非常广泛。

sentences.en: It was among the highest performing articles on social media that day.
sentences.zh: 它是那天社交媒体上表现最好的文章之一。

sentences.en: It's been getting wall-to-wall coverage on Fox News and from other right-wing media outlets.
sentences.zh: 福克斯新闻和其他右翼媒体对其进行了全方位的报道。

sentences.en: So in that sense, if the goal was to reduce the visibility of the story, I think the answer is that no, it didn't stop this story from getting out or being discussed and may have,
sentences.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，如果目标是降低这篇报道的能见度，我认为答案是没有，它没能阻止这篇报道传播或被讨论，甚至可能

sentences.en: in fact, drawn more attention to it than it otherwise would have gotten.
sentences.zh: 事实上，比它原本可能获得的关注还要多。

sentences.en: But I think the thing that did change is the kind of attention that was being paid to the story.
sentences.zh: 但我认为确实发生了变化的是人们对这篇报道的关注方式。

sentences.en: And it represents, I think, a real break from 2016 when the story became all about the emails, all about John Podesta and the DNC and Hillary Clinton, when we were late, frankly,
sentences.zh: 我认为这代表着与2016年的真正决裂——当时，这篇报道完全变成了关于电子邮件、关于约翰·波德斯塔、DNC和希拉里·克林顿的事情，坦白说，我们当时太晚

sentences.en: to turn our attention to the bigger story behind that story, which was that Russia was trying to interfere in our election.
sentences.zh: 才将注意力转向该报道背后的宏大故事，即俄罗斯正试图干预我们的选举。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So a bit messily and with some high-profile reversals, with plenty of angry partisans,
sentences.zh: 因此，伴随着一些混乱、一些备受瞩目的立场反转、大量愤怒的党派支持者，

sentences.en: and with a story that was supposed to be losing steam that has definitely made its way around the internet,
sentences.zh: 以及一篇本该失去势头却在互联网上大肆传播的报道，

sentences.en: we are seeing some meaningful improvements in this social media system over 2016.
sentences.zh: 我们看到相比2016年，这个社交媒体系统有了一些有意义的改进。

sentences.en: — Yeah, I think we are.
sentences.zh: ——是的，我想我们确实看到了。

sentences.en: And all of this is super messy and complicated, and there will no doubt continue to be mistakes and reversals and people claiming partisan bias and threats to free speech.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切都极其混乱和复杂，毫无疑问，未来仍将不断出现错误、立场反转，以及人们对党派偏见和言论自由受到威胁的指责。

sentences.en: — All of that's going to continue.
sentences.zh: ——所有这些都将继续下去。

sentences.en: And, you know, there are still two weeks until the election, so we don't know what could happen between now and then.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，距离选举还有两周，所以我们不知道从现在到那时之间会发生什么。

sentences.en: But right now, I think the big picture is that we are all now much more aware of how we can be manipulated, whether we are executives at a social platform like Facebook, Twitter,
sentences.zh: 但就目前而言，我认为大局是，我们现在都更加清楚我们是如何被操纵的，无论我们是像Facebook、Twitter

sentences.en: or YouTube, whether it's us as journalists at the New York Times, or whether it's just voters, people who consume the news and are trying to make sense of what's happening.
sentences.zh: 或YouTube这样的社交平台高管，还是我们作为《纽约时报》的记者，又或是作为选民、那些消费新闻并试图理解正在发生的事情的人。

sentences.en: I think we are all now much more conscious than we were in 2016 of all of the ways that we could be manipulated or tricked or baited or taken advantage of.
sentences.zh: 我认为，与2016年相比，我们现在对所有可能操纵、欺骗、诱导或利用我们的方式都有了更高的意识。

sentences.en: And I think that increased awareness, that consciousness of the risks that we face, is a good thing, no matter what happens with any one particular story.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这种意识的提高、对我们所面临风险的清醒认识是一件好事，无论某一篇具体的报道最终结果如何。

sentences.en: — Thank you, Kevin.
sentences.zh: ——谢谢你，凯文。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: — Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: ——谢谢邀请。

sentences.en: — We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: ——我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: — On Tuesday, the U.S.
sentences.zh: ——周二，美国

sentences.en: Department of Justice sued Google for allegedly violating antitrust law, accusing it of maintaining an illegal monopoly over search and search advertising.
sentences.zh: 司法部对Google提起诉讼，指控其违反反垄断法，指控其在搜索和搜索广告领域维持非法垄断地位。

sentences.en: The lawsuit represents the most significant legal challenge to a tech company's market power in a generation.
sentences.zh: 这起诉讼代表了一代人对科技公司市场支配地位最具冲击力的法律挑战。

sentences.en: — Google achieved some success in its early years, and no one begrudges that.
sentences.zh: ——Google在其发展的早期取得了一些成功，没有人对此感到嫉妒。

sentences.en: But as the antitrust complaint filed today explains, it has maintained its monopoly power through exclusionary practices that are harmful to competition.
sentences.zh: 但正如今天提交的反垄断诉讼所解释的那样，它通过损害竞争的排他性做法维持了其垄断地位。

sentences.en: The lawsuit accuses Google and its parent company of using exclusive business contracts and agreements to lock out rivals.
sentences.zh: 该诉讼指控Google及其母公司利用独家商业合同和协议来排挤竞争对手。

sentences.en: One such contract paid Apple billions of dollars to make Google the default search engine for iPhones.
sentences.zh: 其中一项合同向苹果支付了数十亿美元，使Google成为iPhone的默认搜索引擎。

sentences.en: As a result, the lawsuit said, both competition and innovation suffered.
sentences.zh: 诉讼称，其结果是竞争和创新都受到了损害。

sentences.en: — So the Justice Department has determined that an antitrust response is necessary to benefit consumers.
sentences.zh: ——因此司法部断定，有必要做出反垄断回应来造福消费者。

sentences.en: If the government does not enforce the antitrust laws to enable competition, we could lose the next wave of innovation.
sentences.zh: 如果政府不执行反垄断法以实现竞争，我们可能会失去下一波创新浪潮。

sentences.en: If that happens, Americans may never get to see the next Google.
sentences.zh: 如果发生这种情况，美国人可能永远也见不到下一个Google了。

sentences.en: — In a statement, Google called the lawsuit deeply flawed and said that rather than helping consumers, it would hurt them.
sentences.zh: ——在一份声明中，Google称该诉讼存在严重缺陷，并表示它不仅无助于消费者，反而会伤害消费者。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: — This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: ——本周的《Wirecutter秀》中，我们正在为假期招待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人们宾至如归的妙招。

sentences.en: — Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: ——他们是黑夜睡眠者吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they black out to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们会不会为了睡觉而失去知觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on The New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 请在《纽约时报》App或你常用的任何播客平台上搜索《Wirecutter秀》。
